title: Worktree setup
summary: Shell commands that keep parallel work tidy: one parked trunk checkout per project, and a worktree beside it for each goal, made with one command.

explain.what: The worktree setup is a set of zsh commands from ACS's own worktree toolkit (installed with acs install-worktree). Each project gets a trunk: a checkout parked on its base branch (main or staging) that nobody works in, which also holds the project's git-ignored env files. Each piece of work gets its own git worktree beside the trunk, on a branch named for the goal and cut from the latest base. A .worktrees.conf file at the trunk records where worktrees go and what they copy. It works in zsh only.
explain.does: wtinit sets a project up once. wnew <name> makes a new worktree in the right place from a fresh base, copies the env files from the trunk so it runs, claims a free port, and prints a banner with the path, branch, base and local address. wls lists a project's worktrees and flags any living outside the expected place. Other commands (wgo, wrm, wclean, wenv) move between, remove and tidy worktrees.
changes: ~/.config/worktree/wt.zsh and defaults.conf (or under $WT_HOME): the toolkit; a differing file is backed up first, and a defaults.conf you customised is kept
~/.zshrc (or $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc): a marked block (# >>> agent-config-studio worktree tools >>> … # <<< agent-config-studio worktree tools <<<) that loads wt.zsh
~/.agent-config-studio/worktree-source/: a copy of the installed toolkit files, used to notice later updates
~/.agent-config-studio/backups/<time>-worktree/: copies of any file it replaced
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes the marked block from your .zshrc and the toolkit files it copied. Your project list in ~/.config/worktree/repos/, your projects, their trunks and their worktrees are never touched. If your shell is not zsh, the setup does nothing, and ACS says so instead of showing it as installed.
